title: State Modules, Async Jobs, and Operations
objective: Choose state-aware modules and control long-running fleet work.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge companion material; no book prose is reproduced.

paragraphs: Package, service, user, file, copy, fetch, cron, and git modules describe resources idempotently. command and shell execute procedures and need extra care around changed status.
async starts long work with a time budget and poll controls whether Ansible waits. Background jobs require later status checks; logs remain essential for diagnosing distributed failures.
explanation.rule: Operational rule: Choose state-aware modules and control long-running fleet work.

examples.title: Working design artifact
examples.code:
operation:
  module: ansible.builtin.package
  state: present
  async_seconds: 600
  poll: 0
examples.note: Use this as a reasoning model before applying changes to the disposable lab.

checks.question: Which statement best matches “State Modules, Async Jobs, and Operations”?
options: Choose state-aware modules and control long-running fleet work.
Make every change with an unreviewed shell command.
Store all secrets in plaintext inventory.

feedback.correct: Correct—the workflow keeps intent and verification explicit.
feedback.incorrect: Review the lesson objective and operational rule.

checks.question: A package is already present and the same state-aware task runs again. What is the healthy result?

feedback.correct: Correct—the desired state is already satisfied, so no change is required.
feedback.incorrect: A state-aware module should report success without changing an already-correct host.

lab.title: Mission: prove privilege escalation and idempotence
lab.setup: Use the Terminal tab after the fleet inspection mission succeeds.
steps: Predict the result, then try installing curl on webservers without --become.
Repeat with --become and confirm the package task succeeds.
Run the identical command again and inspect the changed field.
lab.success: The second successful run reports changed=false for both webservers.
